findings.quoted_text: Contractor will accommodate reasonable changes to scope requested by Client within the overall project budget. Changes that would exceed that budget are documented in a written change request.
The parties intend to allow 15 rounds of ordinary revisions for the principal creative Deliverables. Additional revisions may require a written change order.

findings.explanation: You are required to accept scope changes and perform extra work without additional pay as long as they fit within the overall project budget.
findings.suggested_change: Any changes to the scope of work requested by the Client that alter the agreed Deliverables or increase the workload will be documented in a written change request and billed at the Contractor's standard rates or as mutually agreed.

findings.quoted_text: The parties intend to allow 15 rounds of ordinary revisions for the principal creative Deliverables. Additional revisions may require a written change order.
findings.explanation: The contract allows 15 rounds of revisions, which is excessive and can trap you in endless work without extra compensation.
findings.suggested_change: The parties will include up to 2 rounds of revisions for the principal creative Deliverables. Additional revisions will be billed at the Contractor's standard hourly rate.

findings.explanation: Net 60 payment terms require you to wait up to 60 days to get paid, which can create significant cash flow challenges for your business.
findings.suggested_change: Invoices are payable Net 30 from the date of the invoice.

findings.explanation: The contract permits 15 rounds of revisions, which exposes you to excessive unpaid iteration work.
findings.suggested_change: The Client is entitled to up to three rounds of revisions per Deliverable, and any additional rounds will be charged at the Contractor's standard hourly rate.

findings.explanation: Payment is due 60 days after invoicing, which ties up your cash flow for an extended period.
findings.suggested_change: Payment terms are Net 30 from the invoice date.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body: Hello, thank you for sharing the agreement. I have reviewed the terms and would like to propose a few adjustments before we sign: - Regarding the clause addressing scope changes, the text requires accepting scope changes and performing extra work without additional pay within the project budget; I propose modifying this so that any changes to the scope of work requested by the Client that alter the agreed Deliverables or increase the workload will be documented in a written change request and billed at the Contractor's standard rates or as mutually agreed. - Concerning the clause allowing 15 rounds of ordinary revisions, this is excessive and can trap me in endless work without extra compensation; I propose that the parties will include up to 2 rounds of revisions for the principal creative Deliverables, with additional revisions billed at the Contractor's standard hourly rate. - Regarding the Net 60 payment terms, waiting up to 60 days to get paid can create significant cash flow challenges for my business; I propose that invoices are payable Net 30 from the date of the invoice. - Concerning the revision allowance of 15 rounds, this exposes me to excessive unpaid iteration work; I propose that the Client is entitled to up to three rounds of revisions per Deliverable, and any additional rounds will be charged at the Contractor's standard hourly rate. - Regarding the payment period of Net 60, this ties up cash flow for an extended period; I propose that payment terms are Net 30 from the invoice date. Thank you for your time and flexibility, and I look forward to moving forward.
